title: Review of RV-05 physical action execution refactor
rationale: The proposed physical-action path bypasses mandatory Guardrails and Executor ownership, loses idempotency across restart, treats a missing observation timestamp as fresh, and lacks the required automated and supervised evidence. These are reachable safety defects and required physical-action evidence remains NOT RUN.
scope_architecture: Changed-path inventory: app/control.py introduces a direct watering privilege boundary; app/executor.py introduces process-local acknowledgement state; app/guardrails.py introduces a 300-second freshness runtime default. No persisted/public fields, required environment variables, migration revisions, or operating-system-specific behavior are shown. The direct Control-to-adapter call violates the required Control candidate -> deterministic Guardrails -> idempotent Executor -> approved/fake adapter ownership path. No registered SP-FAIL entry directly captures these new physical-action defects.

findings.finding: A watering suggestion calls the adapter directly, bypassing both deterministic Guardrails and the Executor.
findings.evidence: The added Control function invokes adapter.water from untrusted suggestion fields without a guardrail decision or Executor command transition.
findings.impact: An unvalidated or unbounded suggestion can directly cause a physical watering action without the mandatory safety and idempotency boundaries.
findings.required_change: Route every suggestion through deterministic validation, an explicit Guardrails decision, and the idempotent Executor before invoking an approved or fake adapter.
findings.suggested_test: Test allowed, blocked, malformed, missing, and out-of-range watering suggestions through the complete Guardrails and Executor path using a fake adapter.

findings.finding: Acknowledgement deduplication exists only in process memory and is recorded only after adapter delivery.
findings.evidence: ACKNOWLEDGED is a module-local set; a restart clears it, and a crash after adapter.send but before set.add leaves the same command eligible for another physical send.
findings.impact: Restart or uncertain execution can repeat an already delivered watering command and cause duplicate actuation.
findings.required_change: Persist an atomic idempotency and execution-state transition before delivery, then handle acknowledgement, timeout, late acknowledgement, retry, crash, and restart without replaying an uncertain action.
findings.suggested_test: Simulate a crash before and after adapter delivery, restart the Executor, redeliver the same command, and verify the fake adapter receives at most one physical action.

findings.finding: A state with no observed_at timestamp is assigned age zero and accepted as fresh.
findings.evidence: The missing-timestamp branch returns 0 seconds of age, so state_is_fresh returns true for an input whose freshness cannot be established.
findings.impact: Unknown or stale telemetry can authorize a physical action because the active safety gate treats missing evidence as current.
findings.required_change: Reject missing, malformed, future, timezone-ambiguous, stale, contradictory, or low-confidence state before any action is authorized.
findings.suggested_test: Test missing, null, malformed, naive, future, boundary-age, stale, and low-confidence observations and verify every uncertain state blocks the fake action.

findings.finding: The required supervised safe-hardware and restart rehearsal evidence is NOT RUN.
findings.evidence: The physical_action and production_availability flags require supervised safe-hardware, abort/rollback, restart, and observable recovery evidence; the report explicitly leaves that evidence pending.
findings.evidence_excerpt: NOT RUN: supervised safe-hardware and restart rehearsal
findings.impact: Automation cannot establish safe real-device behavior, abort ownership, restart recovery, or rollback for this physical-action change.
findings.required_change: Complete and record the human-owned supervised safe-hardware, abort, restart, rollback, and post-rollback health procedure before approval.
findings.suggested_test: manual: Have the named hardware/operations owner exercise one bounded fake-or-safe command, abort, restart, rollback, and post-rollback health check under physical supervision.

findings.finding: The generic unit-test claim does not provide the named physical-action failure-path evidence required by the matrix.
findings.evidence: No inspectable results are supplied for allowed/blocked Guardrails, duplicate delivery, retry, timeout, late acknowledgement, restart, stale/low-confidence input, storage failure, or recovery behavior.
findings.evidence_excerpt: PASS: unit tests and fake-adapter CI
findings.impact: Critical duplicate, uncertainty, stale-state, and persistence failures can remain undetected despite a reported green unit suite.
findings.required_change: Add and report explicit behavior-focused results for every required physical-action failure path, plus the full baseline and quality checks.
findings.suggested_test: Run deterministic fake-adapter tests for allowed and blocked Guardrails, duplicate, retry, timeout, late acknowledgement, restart, stale and low-confidence state, storage failure, and observable recovery.

contract_consumer_review: The proposed action suggestion and command identifiers cross Control, Guardrails, Executor, storage, and adapter boundaries, but the artifacts do not define a versioned action contract, units or bounds for seconds, command identity semantics, persistence ownership, or consumer behavior. No edge/network contract change is demonstrated, so SP-FAIL-006 is not selected; adapter execution still requires bounded disconnected-device and timeout evidence under the selected edge_hardware_integration class.

evidence_matrix.check: All three patch artifact SHA-256 values match the case metadata
Reported unit tests and fake-adapter CI
Named Guardrails, duplicate, retry, timeout, late-ACK, restart, stale, low-confidence, and storage-failure tests
Full pytest and lint, format, and type baseline
Supervised safe-hardware, abort, restart, rollback, and post-rollback health rehearsal

operations_safety_security_privacy: The change reaches the physical adapter, has no durable idempotency state, and fails open on absent freshness metadata. No production access, external export, migration, credential, or public-data change is shown. Manual hardware and availability evidence is explicitly pending, and no safe rollback or observable uncertain-execution recovery is supplied.
documentation_assessment: No action-contract, persistence-state, operator abort, restart recovery, or rollback documentation is included in the reviewed artifacts. Current-state documentation says active Executor/hardware command delivery is not implemented, so this capability cannot be presented as current without a separately approved design and synchronized documentation.
limitations: Review was limited to the approved evaluation case, mandatory stable rule pack, reviewer contract, report schema, and the three hash-verified named patch artifacts.
No CI logs, full test bodies, runtime environment, production data, private infrastructure, real hardware, or implementation files outside the supplied patches were inspected.
Reported PASS statuses reflect supplied claims only; no tests or hardware procedures were executed by the reviewer.
